extracted.intended_audience: Office of Medical Services (OMS) management and planning officials; CIA planning staff (Chief, Plans Staff, DDS)
extracted.subtask_description: Internal CIA memorandum describing OMS goals and planned actions to implement OMB Circular A-44 (Revised), focusing on management effectiveness, program planning, and cost reduction for medical services over a six-month planning period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Effectiveness Goals — Improved operating efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve operating efficiency by bringing OMS division and staff chiefs more effectively into the program planning process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum states this is a continuation of a practice already started: involving OMS division and staff chiefs (who are MDs or PhDs with professional expertise) in PPB-type program planning which requires special attention. During January and part of February 1971 OMS will draft the OMS Program Plan for FY 1973-1977; division and staff chiefs will work closely with planning officials and contribute to a greater degree than before. The anticipated result is a program submission with significant contributions from these officials and improved future planning and operating efficiency due to the experience they receive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program planning participation and development of OMS Program Plan (FY 1973-1977)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a draft OMS Program Plan (FY 1973-1977) with substantive contributions from division and staff chiefs within the stated timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline: January and part of February 1971 for drafting. Emphasizes close collaboration between division/staff chiefs and planning officials to ensure the program submission reflects wide contribution. The process is framed as a management-development tool: participation will train officials in program planning and thereby improve future efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Reduction Goals — Reduction in unit cost for laboratory testing materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce unit costs for laboratory testing materials by adopting automated multiphasic biochemical profiling (SMA 12 Jr.) in the Clinical Division laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational/technical details provided as justification: the SMA 12 Jr. runs 12 tests on one blood sample and can process ~30 samples per hour. Reagent costs for a battery of 12 automated tests are ~$2 versus $12 if the 12 tests were run manually (manual reagents cost ~$1 per test), yielding roughly one-sixth reagent cost of the previous procedure. The memorandum frames such economies as enabling multiphasic screening programs intended to make services accessible to more Agency employees. This entry includes throughput, per-test reagent cost comparisons, and the programmatic aim to extend access through screening.
